raw.Narrative:
On September [XXX], 2025 at 1:21 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in Tempe, Arizona was in a collision involving a motorcycle on [XXX] at [XXX]. 
The Waymo AV was traveling north in the rightmost lane on [XXX] and began slowing with its right turn signal activated in preparation for a right turn into a parking lot at [XXX], yielding to a pedestrian crossing the driveway entrance to the parking lot on the right-hand sidewalk. While the Waymo AV was slowing with its right turn signal activated, a motorcycle in the rightmost lane approached the Waymo AV from behind and the front of the motorcycle made contact with the rear left corner of the Waymo AV. The impact with the Waymo AV resulted in the motorcyclist falling from the motorcycle and into the roadway to the left of the Waymo AV. Immediately afterwards, a passenger car in the second-from-the-rightmost lane passed the Waymo AV on the left and struck the motorcyclist in the roadway. The passenger car did not stop and left the scene. The motorcyclist was transported from the scene to a hospital, where they were declared deceased. At the time of impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and the Waymo AV was not carrying passengers. Following contact with the motorcycle, the Waymo AV came to a complete stop and remained stopped until the vehicle was towed away several hours later. The Waymo AV and the motorcycle sustained damage. The extent of the damage to the passenger car that left the scene is unknown at this time.
Waymo is reporting this crash under Request No. 1 of Standing General Order 2021-01 because of a fatality. Waymo may supplement or correct its reporting with additional information as it may become available.

On June [XXX], 2026 at 1:07 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was involved in a collision involving a motorcycle and an SUV on [XXX] at [XXX].  

The Waymo AV was stopped in the dedicated left turn lane for a red light on [XXX] at the intersection with [XXX]. While the Waymo AV remained stopped, a motorcycle traveling in the second from the right lane came to a stop adjacent to an SUV that was stopped in the rightmost lane. After both vehicles briefly remained stopped, the SUV and motorcycle began to proceed forward when the SUV changed lanes into the second from the right lane, towards the motorcycle. The motorcycle maneuvered left towards the dedicated left turn lane, and the SUV continued to change lanes across the second from the right lane, towards the motorcycle into the dedicated left turn lane. While the SUV continued to change lanes, the front right of the SUV made contact with the rear of the motorcycle, and the front left of the SUV made contact with the right side of a passenger car that was stopped behind the Waymo AV. As a result of this initial contact with the SUV, the motorcycle continued forward and the front of the motorcycle then made contact with the rear right of the Waymo AV. The SUV also continued forward, and the front left of the SUV then made contact with the rear right of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. All involved vehicles sustained damage, and the motorcyclist was transported to the hospital by ambulance with unknown injuries.

Waymo is reporting this crash under Request No. 1 of Standing General Order 2021-01 because an individual involved was transported from the scene to a hospital by ambulance. Waymo may supplement or correct its reporting with additional information as it may become available.

raw.Narrative: During normal autonomous operation, the May autonomous shuttle (Ego) was traveling through a narrow section of roadway in a parking lot bordered by parked vehicles on the left and a retaining wall on the right on experimental software version v29.0.20. As the Ego proceeded, the system initially recognized the static retaining wall as a large, non-rectangular object. As the Ego approaches the wall, the resulting density of lidar returns on the object (wall) exceeds the detectors maximum limitation. The newer lidar points, toward the forward edge of the elongated object, exceeding the limit were filtered out, causing the track to disappear when the ego approached 5m from the track (i.e. the wall). The situation was exacerbated by the fact that the road edge was incorrectly marked in that section.  The road edge was drawn through the retaining wall and thus the vehicle did not have any prior knowledge about the edge of the road. As a result, the Ego drove too close to the wall, scraping it at a speed of 2 meters per second while driving straight (i.e. in lane-nominal policy) with no nudge or veer corrections. There was no damage to the wall. The limitation leading to the lost track affects Software versions v26.0 (when the Open World Tracklet v2 feature was introduced) through v31.0. This is the only known instance of this failure mode, and in v32.0 an optimization was made to remove the LIDAR threshold entirely and mitigate the vulnerability.  Furthermore, the incorrect road edge annotation was corrected shortly after this incident and the map updated for the deployed vehicles.

raw.Narrative: The May Mobility vehicle (Ego) is stopped at a red light, then the Ego begins to accelerate and turn right when the traffic light changes to green. As the Ego accelerates, a pedestrian begins moving and enters the crosswalk from the other side of the intersection. This activates the rule-based crosswalk logic. Ego determines that it is able to stop before the crosswalk without exceeding our max deceleration threshold, which triggers an in-policy stopping reaction for the crosswalk. The Ego brakes to yield for the pedestrian. The vehicle trailing the Ego accelerates, making contact with the rear-end of the Ego. In the 2.5 seconds between the start of the Ego braking and the collision, the rear vehicle accelerated from 0.2 to 6.1 m/s (0.4 to 13.6 mph) without slowing until after the collision occurred. raw.Narrative: The May Mobility vehicle (Ego) approaches a turn with a trailing vehicle following closely behind. The May planner initially selects a trajectory it believes will safely complete the turn. However, as the Ego begins the turn, it re-evaluates the situation and detects a significant risk of striking the curb. At that point, the planner shifts focus from avoiding the curb entirely to minimizing the severity of a potential curb strike. To reduce speed before the expected contact, the Ego brakes at 3.5 m/sÂ²). Because the trailing vehicle is following so closely, this deceleration makes a rear-end collision likely. The Ego predicts a potential rear-end collision and elects to reduce brake force to lessen the impact severity. Moments later, the trailing vehicle strikes the rear driver-side bumper of the Ego and then drives away. Future improvements are underway to give the planner a policy option to steer away from curbs. This new capability will help the vehicle avoid situations where braking becomes the only remaining way to manage close curb proximity.

raw.Narrative:
The [XXX] was driving on [XXX] towards [XXX] in Riverside California. A minivan reversed out of a parking position (perpendicular parking to road lane) from the right side of the road into the shuttle¢ÂÂs path and struck the shuttle from the side.
After the incident a supervisor from the Riverside Transport Agency RTA (operator or the vehicle) was called to the side. The RTA supervisor recorded the incident according to RTAs protocols.
In addition to the [XXX] trainer/supervisor being on the vehicle additional [XXX] personal was called to the side as well.

Summary of Events:
-Upon detecting the minivan in the side envelope, the system issued a brake command within 5ms.
-Brake pressure began rising 58ms after the command and exceeded 90% of the requested pressure 164ms after the initial command.
-The minivan reversed out of a parking space perpendicular to the [XXX] Ã¢ÂÂs direction of travel and struck the Lift on the side.
-The minivan continued reversing until contact occurred.
-The elapsed time from first detection of the minivan in the side envelope to impact was approximately 358ms.
-The vehicle came to a complete stop in 1.178 seconds.

In Summary:
The other car pushing out from the parking position did not give way as would have been required.
The [XXX] detected the other car getting into the right side of its safety envelope just 358ms before the impact. The reaction time of the [XXX] was as expected in terms of reacting to the signal and initiating a brake maneuver. However, the short time and distance between the other car entering the [XXX] safety envelope (and consequently its track) was too short to avoid the collision. Even if the [XXX] had come to a complete stop before the actual impact the collision would most likely have happened but potentially at a slightly different position.

On July [XXX], 2026, at approximately 10:54 AM PDT, a MOIA autonomous vehicle ("MOIA AV") was operating in autonomous mode in Beverly Hills, California, with a safety driver in the driver's seat.

The MOIA AV was traveling southbound on [XXX] and completed a left turn onto eastbound [XXX]. As the MOIA AV proceeded eastbound approaching the intersection with [XXX], the automated driving system disengaged. Approximately nine seconds after the disengagement, and with the automated driving system no longer in control, the safety driver allowed the MOIA AV to drift to the right causing the front passenger side of the MOIA AV to make contact with the driver side of a passenger car that was parked and unoccupied at the south curb of [XXX], facing east. The MOIA AV was traveling at approximately 19 mph at the time of contact. At the time of contact, the MOIA AV's automated driving system was not engaged. Following the contact, the safety driver brought the MOIA AV to a controlled stop at the curb ahead of the parked vehicle.

No injuries were reported. The parked vehicle was unoccupied at the time of contact. No airbags deployed. Both vehicles sustained minor damage, and neither vehicle was towed from the scene. Weather conditions were clear, and the roadway surface was dry. The registered owner of the parked vehicle was notified of the collision at the scene and provided appropriate contact and insurance information. Law enforcement was not contacted.

MOIA is reporting this crash under Request No. 2 of Standing General Order 2021-01 because the subject vehicle struck another vehicle, and the automated driving system was engaged within the 30 seconds immediately prior to the crash. MOIA is reviewing the vehicle data and may supplement or correct this report as additional information becomes available.
